message.content: A computer processes information through a complex, synchronized dance of hardware and software components, all orchestrated by the central processing unit (CPU). The processor is the brain of the computer, responsible for executing instructions and performing calculations. It operates by fetching data from memory, decoding the instructions, and then executing them. This cycle, known as the fetch-decode-execute cycle, happens billions of times per second. The processor uses transistors, microscopic switches that represent binary states of 0 and 1, to perform logical operations. These operations are grouped into instruction sets, which allow the computer to perform tasks ranging from simple arithmetic to complex graphical rendering
